details:
APOLLO V – Project Details

APOLLO V is an interactive web-based space mission design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 – Space Mission Design Game challenge. It gives players the opportunity to experience the role of a space mission planner and explore the challenges of designing and managing a mission to the Moon.

How It Works

The game takes players through the main stages of a lunar mission. Players begin by learning the game mechanics and exploring the mission objectives. They then experience rocket design, mission preparation, launch, spaceflight, and lunar exploration through interactive gameplay.

The rocket design experience introduces important components such as payload, rocket structure, propulsion systems, boosters, and power systems. Players explore how different design choices and resource limitations can affect mission performance.

The game also introduces the challenges of spacecraft navigation and lunar landing, helping players understand that a successful space mission requires careful planning and decision-making.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our main goal is to make space exploration and aerospace engineering concepts easier to understand and more engaging, especially for students and beginners.

APOLLO V aims to:

  • Introduce players to the basic principles of rocket design and space mission planning.
  • Demonstrate the importance of managing resources and making engineering decisions.
  • Encourage critical thinking, problem-solving, and experimentation.
  • Make learning about space exploration more interactive and enjoyable.
  • Inspire young people to explore science, technology, and aerospace engineering.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the project as a web-based game using modern development technologies:

  • Visual Studio Code: Code editor.
  • Node.js and npm: Development environment and package management.
  • Vite: Development server and build tool.
  • TypeScript: Programming language.
  • React: User interface development.
  • Tailwind CSS: Interface styling.
  • Zustand: Game state management.
  • Framer Motion: Animations and transitions.
  • Canvas 2D: 2D graphics rendering.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and collaboration.

The project is software-based and does not require additional physical hardware.

NASA Resources

We used NASA images as visual resources to support the game's space exploration environment and connect the experience with real-world space exploration.

One of our reference sources is the official NASA Images and Video Library:
https://images.nasa.gov/

These images help create an engaging visual experience and strengthen the connection between the game and actual space exploration.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative idea behind APOLLO V is to turn the complex process of planning a lunar mission into an interactive experience. Instead of presenting players with technical information alone, the game allows them to explore mission decisions through gameplay.

We combine educational concepts, game mechanics, visual storytelling, and interactive design to make space mission planning more accessible to a wider audience.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors when designing the experience:

  • Accessibility: Making the game understandable for beginners.
  • Educational Value: Connecting gameplay with real space mission concepts.
  • Resource Management: Showing how engineering choices involve limitations and trade-offs.
  • User Experience: Keeping the interface clear and the gameplay engaging.
  • Visual Quality: Using space-related imagery and animations to create an immersive environment.
  • Technical Feasibility: Building a web-based experience that can be accessed without specialized hardware.

Conclusion

APOLLO V aims to bring space mission planning closer to players by combining technology, education, and interactive gameplay. Through this project, we hope to encourage curiosity, develop problem-solving skills, and inspire the next generation to explore the possibilities of space science and engineering.
